term: finite hitting, finite possible population and compact profile space
definition: Hitting p supplies a finite list with at least one member concretely present at each admissible world. It need not bound the union of populations. OneFinite p supplies one world with a Mathlib-finite population; it need not make all populations finite. component W is universal accessibility on the supplied inhabited component; an explicit actual w rules out empty-world-type vacuity. profilePresent S x v is v.val x = true in the product of discrete Bool spaces. K is actual Mathlib IsCompact S, not an assumed possible limit, finite consistency or an epistemic possibility rule. NoNecessary is the negation of the existing DeRe, with no change to candidate identity.
note: Analyst formulations #561; attribution deferred. Semantic meaning, examples, rival and open applicability burdens are in docs/notes/finite-hitting-561.md. Absence amalgamation remains the existing explicitly stipulated subset-of-intersection policy, not exact meet closure or a temporal operation. Necessarily concrete here does not imply God, uniqueness, underived ground or cause.
